your_book:
Jaleel's book had a decent Wednesday, September 2, lifted primarily by NVIDIA's +3.21% surge — its ~9.8% weight making it the single biggest contributor on the day. Abbott (10.6% weight, +1.41%) and Danaher (+1.44%) added steady ballast, while Vertex Pharma (+1.66%) and Lululemon (+1.75%) chipped in from smaller positions. On the other side, Adobe slid 2.20% — worth noting given its 5.6% weight and an earnings event on September 10 looming — and Zoetis dropped 1.40%, deepening an already -3.3% unrealized loss on a position that carries a BUY verdict but continues to drift the wrong direction. SPGI fell 1.93% and is now essentially flat on the unrealized basis, a position that hasn't rewarded patience yet.

The clearest thesis-vs.-price tension sits in three names. Rocket Lab (6.3% weight) carries an AVOID verdict yet remains in the book at -19.5% unrealized — that gap between conviction and action is the sharpest divergence in the portfolio and warrants a hard look. BSX is rated STRONG BUY despite a guidance slash (FY26 growth cut from 10.5% to 7–8.5%) and is slightly underwater; the model likes it but management has already walked numbers down once. LULU reports tomorrow (September 3) with an elevated risk flag — Americas comps -5% for five straight quarters and margin pressure from tariffs — and today's +1.75% pop into earnings is a setup worth watching carefully.

The pharma cluster (AZN, GILD, NVS, NBIX, VRTX) faces a quiet but persistent drug-pricing overhang from MFN deals and import tariffs; no single name is alarming, but the collective weight is meaningful. NVDA's headline risk around export controls and AI-capex sentiment hasn't gone away — today's gain is welcome, but the watch flag is still active heading into any macro catalyst on semiconductor policy.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated at -19.5% — thesis and position are in direct conflict
attention.note: Rocket Lab carries an explicit AVOID verdict yet holds a 6.3% weight with a nearly 20% unrealized loss; a capital-preservation mandate makes this the most urgent unresolved contradiction in Jaleel's book.

attention.headline: Earnings tomorrow (Sep 3) into an elevated risk flag
attention.note: Five consecutive negative Americas comp quarters, tariff-gutted margins, and a guidance-cut flag mean tomorrow's report is a genuine binary event for a position already -6.1% unrealized.

attention.headline: Earnings September 10 — narrative risk, not just numbers
attention.note: Adobe fell 2.20% today and its risk flag notes the stock sells off on AI-moat fears even when it beats; at 5.6% weight, another post-earnings drawdown would be felt across the book.

attention.headline: STRONG BUY verdict vs. slashed guidance and underwater position
attention.note: Management already cut FY26 growth guidance from 10.5% to 7–8.5% and guided flat through Q3, yet the model rates it STRONG BUY — the divergence between model conviction and fundamental momentum deserves scrutiny before the October 28 update.
